lessons.title: I want, I have
lessons.subtitle: Your first sentences: person + action + thing.
notes: Question: put **ma** at the end.
Not want: **bú yào**.
Not have: **méi yǒu** (never bù yǒu).
To answer yes, repeat the action: **yào** (yes, I want) or **yǒu** (yes, I have).
To answer no: **bú yào** or **méi yǒu**.

lessons.title: Is, are, my, your
lessons.subtitle: Say who people are and who owns what.
lessons.pattern: A + shì + B   |   Owner + de + Thing
notes: **men** makes people plural: wǒ + men = wǒmen (we). Never use it for things.
Not: **bú shì**.
wǒ de = my, nǐ de = your, tā de = his, wǒmen de = our.
Yes = **shì**. No = **bú shì**.
Drop the thing to say mine, yours: zhège shì **wǒ de** = this is mine.

lessons.title: What, who, where
lessons.subtitle: Ask questions and say where things are.
lessons.pattern: The question word sits where the answer will go
notes: nǐ yào **shénme**? -> wǒ yào **huò**. Same order, just swap the word.
Do not add ma when you already have a question word.
Where something is: Thing + **zài** + Place. Not: **bú zài**.
**shéi de** = whose: zhège shì shéi de? = whose is this?
**shénme** + thing = what kind of: shénme huò = what goods.

lessons.title: Numbers and prices
lessons.subtitle: Count, ask how much, ask how many.

words.chinese: 七 八 九 十

notes: Big numbers stack up: shíyī = 11, èrshí = 20, wǔshí = 50, sānbǎi = 300, liǎngqiān = 2,000.
Chinese counts in ten-thousands: 50,000 = wǔ wàn.
Use **liǎng** ge for two of something, not èr ge.
yī changes its tone before other words: **yí** ge, **yí** wàn, but **yì**bǎi, **yì**qiān. Copy the audio.
Prices: Thing + Number + kuài. No shì needed: zhège shí kuài = this is 10 yuan.

lessons.title: Buy, sell, pay, send
lessons.subtitle: The action words of trading.
notes: **xiǎng** goes before another action: wǒ xiǎng mǎi = I would like to buy.
Giving: Person + **gěi** + Receiver + Thing.
mǎi (buy) dips low then rises; mài (sell) falls sharply. Listen to both.
Not doing something: **bù** + action (bù mǎi, bú mài, bú fù).
fù goes with qián (pay money); fā goes with huò (send goods).

lessons.title: Good, expensive, cheap
lessons.subtitle: Describe things and react to a price.
notes: Say zhège **hěn** guì. Do not say zhège shì guì.
Not: **bù** + describing word (bú guì, bù hǎo).
Too much: **tài** ... **le**.
Describing word + **de** = the ... one: dà de = the big one, piányi de = the cheap one.
In a ma question drop hěn: zhège guì ma?

lessons.title: Today, tomorrow, done
lessons.subtitle: Say when, and say that something is finished.
notes: Time always comes before the action, never at the end.
Put **le** after the action to show it is done: fù le = paid.
Counting days needs no ge: sān tiān. Months do: liǎng ge yuè.
Did not do it: **méi** + action, and no le: wǒ méi fù = I haven't paid.
Chinese has no will or did. The time word tells you: míngtiān = future, zuótiān = past.

Did not come or go: **méi** lái, **méi** qù.

lessons.title: Speak, understand, can
lessons.subtitle: Handle a real conversation and ask for a better price.
notes: Not: **bù néng**, **bù kěyǐ**, **bù dǒng**, **bù zhīdào**.
**kěyǐ** on its own means OK, fine.
**yìdiǎn** goes after the describing word: piányi yìdiǎn = a bit cheaper.
**tīng bù dǒng** is a fixed phrase: I hear you but can't follow. Use it when someone speaks too fast.
Describing word + **yìdiǎn**: dà yìdiǎn = a bit bigger, piányi yìdiǎn = a bit cheaper.

lessons.title: Joining words and a full conversation
lessons.subtitle: Link ideas, be polite, and run a whole deal.
notes: **yě** and **dōu** go before the action, never at the end.
**hé** joins two things, not two sentences.
**qǐng** goes at the start: qǐng děng yíxià = please wait a moment.
**dōu** needs more than one person or thing before it: wǒmen dōu, tāmen dōu, huò dōu.
Someone says duìbuqǐ, you answer **méi guānxi**.
